title: Teaching elementary students to use word-part clues
population: Grades 3–9 school-text corpus; small Grade 3 instructional comparison
claim: Prioritizes common affixes, proposes meaning-grouped prefix lessons, teaches nonexamples and contextual meaning checks, and reports transfer to unfamiliar words.
limitation: Grade 4–5 placements are historical suggestions, not a comparison establishing the best sequence. Prefix definition is restricted to familiar detachable bases; do not generalize it to bound-base morphology.

title: Exploring How Initial Response to Instruction Predicts Morphology Outcomes Among Students With Decoding Difficulties
claim: Prefix-family lessons included familiar bases, scheduled review, blending/segmenting and meaning mapping; early response helped predict later morphology performance.
limitation: Not a trial comparing teaching orders or proof of an optimal prefix sequence.
tags: Early response; semantic prefix families; review

title: The Importance of Speech-Language Pathologists’ Explicit Knowledge of Morphology
claim: Recommends starting with transparent derived words, then introducing less transparent shifts; illustrates selecting frequent morphemes with a shared grammatical function.
limitation: Clinical reasoning and a hypothetical case, not a controlled intervention-effect study.

title: Morphological Awareness: Connecting Language Foundations and Academic Literacy Success for Students With Language and Literacy Deficits
population: School-age language/literacy deficits; Grade 4 planning example
claim: Links learner needs with grade-level standards and classroom vocabulary to develop individualized objectives and contextualized intervention.
limitation: Illustrative clinical guidance, not evidence that its example goals or sequence are universally effective.

title: Derivational Morphology: An Intervention Forum
claim: Introduces three morphology intervention reports and contrasts delivery, instruction and data collection approaches.
limitation: Overview, not an additional independent intervention trial; do not double-count the studies it introduces.

title: Morphological Interventions to Support Literacy From Kindergarten to Grade 12
claim: Connects developmental expectations and curriculum standards to word analysis, synthesis and meaning-focused teaching across grade levels.
limitation: Tutorial, not a validated fixed grade-by-grade morpheme sequence or product efficacy test.

title: Morphological Awareness Performance Profiles of First- Through Sixth-Grade Students
claim: Different patterns of strengths and weaknesses emerged across morphology tasks; supports sampling multiple task types when selecting targets.
limitation: Not an intervention or teaching-order trial; grade membership does not determine an individual learner’s profile.

title: The Importance of Morphological Awareness in Bilingual Language and Literacy Skills: Clinical Implications for Speech-Language Pathologists
population: Bilingual language and literacy; multiple orthographies
claim: Discusses explicit morphology, language-specific structure, home-language support and appropriate cross-language connections.
limitation: Clinical guidance; do not assume English targets, cognates or transfer apply identically across languages.

title: Reporting of Classroom-Based Morphological Awareness Instruction and Intervention for Kindergarten to Grade 3 Students in the Literature: A Scoping Review
claim: Documents how targets, instructional components and implementation details are reported, supporting explicit descriptions for faithful implementation.
limitation: Reporting review, not an effect-size synthesis or proof of a best instructional order.

title: The Impact of Morphological Intervention on Literacy Knowledge and Reading Motivation: A Cluster-Randomized Comparison Trial in Diverse Socioeconomic Status Kindergartens
claim: Storytelling-based morphology intervention produced gains on measured morphology and print concepts; vocabulary/motivation findings differed by group.
limitation: Hebrew and kindergarten context; not direct validation of an English Grades 2–8 sequence or this app.

title: Toward Understanding the Lexical–Morphological Networks of Children With Specific Language Impairment: Analysis of Responses on a Morphological Production Task
claim: Examines derived-form production and error patterns, informing attention to lexical and morphological knowledge within production tasks.
limitation: Not a treatment trial; group differences do not establish an instructional order or diagnose an individual learner.

title: Predicting Children’s Long-Term Knowledge of Taught Words and Transfer Words After a Morphological Vocabulary Intervention
claim: Examines prediction of later knowledge for taught and transfer words, supporting separate attention to initial response and delayed transfer measurement.
limitation: Predictive analysis in Danish; not a new efficacy trial or an English teaching-order comparison.
tags: Delayed retention; taught versus transfer words

title: Supporting Content and Disciplinary Literacy Success for Adolescents With LLD: A Blended and Contextualized Morphological Awareness Strategy Approach
population: Adolescents with language/literacy deficits; science curriculum
claim: Explains linking explicit morphology and word-meaning strategies to authentic disciplinary vocabulary and text.
limitation: Clinical framework, not a controlled efficacy test or fixed morpheme teaching list.

title: Morphological Development in Normal and Clinical Populations
claim: Reviews morphological processing and the importance of precise lexical representations and relationships between form and meaning.
limitation: Narrative synthesis; does not establish a fixed morpheme order or an intervention effect.

title: Forum: Morphological Awareness as a Key Factor in Language-Literacy Success for Academic Achievement
claim: Connects morphology with phonology, orthography and semantics and introduces assessment and intervention papers in the forum.
limitation: Overview, not an independent treatment study; avoid double-counting the forum studies.

title: Morphological Analysis in Context Versus Isolation: Use of a Dynamic Assessment Task With School-Age Children
population: Typically developing children in Grades 3 and 5
claim: Examines definitions of derived words in isolation and context using graduated support. Performance varied by grade and reading experience.
limitation: The context advantage was not significant after controlling reading frequency; not an intervention effect or a validated app score.

title: A Dynamic Measure of Morphological Awareness and First-Grade Literacy Skill
population: 74 first-grade children with varying language abilities
claim: Provides preliminary evidence for graduated prompting in an early morphology measure and relationships with language/literacy performance.
limitation: First-grade feasibility and prediction evidence; does not validate informal app probes or determine an older learner’s placement.

title: Morphology and Literacy: Getting Our Heads in the Game
claim: Introduces five forum papers covering morphological skills across ages and tasks.
limitation: Background introduction, not a separate intervention trial or evidence for arcade games.

title: Using Morphological Awareness Instruction to Improve Written Language Skills
claim: Reviews morphology and written-language research and illustrates explicit analysis, word construction, word sorts and integration with reading and spelling.
limitation: Tutorial synthesizing earlier work; not an independent test of a fixed instructional order.

title: Morphological Awareness Strategies to Promote Academic Success at Tier 1 Through Interprofessional Collaboration
claim: Describes an eight-week curriculum-connected teacher–SLP collaboration model linking morphology with classroom vocabulary, reading and writing.
limitation: Framework and case illustration; not a controlled trial establishing this app’s Tier 1 efficacy or replacing individualized services.

title: Derivational Morphology: Why It Should Be Included in Language Assessment and Instruction
type: Historical review / proposed scope and sequence
claim: Appendix A proposes morpheme groupings and a progression toward more complex derivations with sound/spelling changes.
limitation: The authors explicitly describe the proposed scope and sequence as speculative; approximate grade suggestions are historical, not current standards or experimentally established placement rules.
tags: Historical sequence proposal; transparency; word-part groupings

title: Deficits in Explicit Language Problem Solving Rather Than in Implicit Learning in Specific Language Impairment: Evidence From Learning an Artificial Morphological Rule
population: 26 children: SLI and typical comparison groups
claim: Distinguishes learning task regularities from explicitly discovering an artificial rule and generalizing it to new items.
limitation: Small laboratory study, not a direct test of classroom morphology instruction or evidence that implicit learning is universally intact in every learner.
tags: Task demands; explicit reasoning versus practiced performance
